construction: Both proof circuits, their complete producer catalogues and the three counter circuits were saved before witness generation. Circuit acceptance checks every reference and the final formula, rather than a circuit hardcoding the chosen proof. The two tiny literal Wang controls are fixed in the saved Source.

The tile checker is independently implemented and checks every compressed row with a 20-case CROSS transport lemma. Literal expansion is independently checked only below its declared 50,000-cell bound; above it the literal checker returns UNKNOWN.

The proof frontend covers an explicitly finite UI/MP/GEN basis with closed assumptions. Its logical rule admission and the circuit compiler remain separate trust obligations; full first-order syntax verification has not yet been compiled into these tiles.

The first attempted study stopped at its initial graph audit: the new auditor omitted explicit zero totals for root points. No positive result was accepted. Its Source, frozen instances and native exit-1 log are preserved. The second attempt corrected that audit, tightened duplicate proof-site binding, and completed with unchanged Source guards.

The two-counter frontend currently has no general compiler resource ceiling. Only the three explicitly frozen small programs were run under a single 180-second observer. Arbitrary large compiler jobs are outside this experiment’s resource claim.
notes: The same exact 100 ordinary Wang tiles check all saved circuits. Arithmetic and symbolic incidence proofs were found automatically in a finite logical producer universe, then lowered to this palette.
This is a fixed-palette backend milestone. The large circuit patches were not searched as literal Wang grids, and there is no RL training or speed-advantage claim in this study.
A separate five-cell literal Wang patch was searched by the unchanged GCTS engine; its impossible fixed-input companion was exhausted. Large CROSS ribbons are reusable certified cluster families.

Each logical search found seven lines. The fixed checker circuits allow eight arithmetic or twelve incidence slots; deterministic repetitions at the start pad shorter proofs. The reader defaults to the original searched proof and can show the exact padded circuit witness.
